I have been competing in organized settings for years and have a clear vision for my top-tier athletic pathway.

When you imagine yourself standing at the start line of The Brisbane 2032 Games, having reached your prime, what is the single biggest evolution you expect to have occurred in your approach to high-performance sport?

A refined, calculated mastery of my technical discipline.

Because you have prioritized competitive history and high-intensity power, your adaptation to this classification will be seamless, turning every stride into a masterclass of force production. scouting_result.scout_verdict:
Where the track demands raw explosion, the slopes demand total mental and physical synchronicity. You have expressed a clear, evolving desire for refined, calculated mastery—a shift from the chaotic burst of power to the surgical precision required to carve an edge through high-speed turns. At 22, heading into The Brisbane 2032 Games, this pathway allows you to transform your competitive discipline into a meditative, high-stakes art form.

Within the LW12 classification—reserved for sit-skiers with lower-limb impairments who utilize a single mono-ski—your focus on technical mastery will shine. Here, the weight of your frame and your ability to maintain core balance become the primary drivers of your speed. This adaptive pathway offers a sophisticated counterpoint to your sprinting, forcing you to read the terrain with a cerebral intensity that creates a unique, balanced excellence. It is the perfect stage to showcase how your hunger for precision can conquer even the most demanding descent at The Brisbane 2032 Games.
